threads.body: [General] `cometds` is the TLS endpoint scheme for the same CometD messaging system, so this currently emits a different `messaging.system` value from `cometd`. Normalize the scheme alias to `cometd` so telemetry for the same system is not split.

replies.body: Fixed in 57932e38256: the `cometds` endpoint alias now reports `messaging.system=cometd`.

threads.body: [General] Eclipse Paho is an MQTT client implementation, not a distinct messaging system. Emitting `messaging.system=paho` fragments MQTT telemetry and contradicts the normalization already applied to aliases such as `sjms`; map this component to `mqtt`.

replies.body: Fixed in 57932e38256: the Paho component now reports `messaging.system=mqtt`.

threads.body: [General] This makes the Camel SQS span keyless/CLIENT, but it does not stop that span from being propagated: `CamelEventNotifier` still unconditionally calls `injectParent`, and Camel 2.20's `SqsProducer` copies every unfiltered string header into SQS message attributes. The message therefore carries a W3C `traceparent` for this CLIENT span in addition to the nested AWS SDK span's `AWSTraceHeader`; consumers using W3C extraction can continue the wrong span. In stable mode, skip Camel's injection when `isMessagingSpanContextPropagated()` is false (while preserving the legacy path), and add an assertion that SQS sends contain only the nested SDK propagation context.

replies.body:
Addressed in 6b98e86c803cc0a0bba60d35a47b8b4aa982f39d.

Analysis: The keyless stable SQS instrumenter prevents semantic suppression but does not control CamelEventNotifier's separate exchange-header injection. Gating that injection for stable messaging requests whose decorator reports no propagation leaves the AWS SDK producer as the sole SQS propagation source, while explicit non-messaging and legacy branches preserve their existing behavior.

Upsides: Stable SQS messages carry the nested AWS SDK `AWSTraceHeader` without a competing Camel `traceparent`; tests inspect the received message and verify both stable suppression and legacy W3C propagation.

Downsides: The SQS test helper now requests all custom message attributes and returns the received message; production behavior for other messaging and non-messaging components is unchanged.

threads.body: [General] Skipping injection does not remove propagation headers already present on the Camel exchange. For example, an HTTP-to-SQS route can retain the inbound `traceparent`; Camel's SQS producer copies string exchange headers into message attributes, so stable mode will still publish that stale W3C context alongside the nested AWS SDK span's `AWSTraceHeader`. Clear the configured propagator fields for non-propagating stable sends (and cover a send whose exchange already contains `traceparent`) so the SDK context is the only creation context carried by SQS.

replies.body:
Addressed in 914823bed9bb441f158371348767434546deebd3.

Analysis: The condition on lines 69-74 correctly skips injecting span context for non-propagating stable messaging sends (e.g., aws-sqs). However, skipping injection leaves any propagation headers already on the exchange in place. In an HTTP-to-SQS route, the inbound `traceparent` header lands on the Camel exchange; the SQS producer then copies all string exchange headers into SQS message attributes. This means a stale W3C trace context travels alongside the AWS SDK's own `AWSTraceHeader`, giving downstream consumers two conflicting creation contexts. The fix adds an else branch that calls `CamelPropagationUtil.clearPropagationFields`, which removes every field the configured TextMapPropagator declares, so non-propagating sends carry no inherited trace context at all.

Upsides: Non-propagating stable messaging sends no longer leak inbound propagation headers into the outbound message carrier. For SQS routes originating from HTTP, the AWS SDK's `AWSTraceHeader` becomes the sole context on the message, matching the semantic intent of `isSpanContextPropagated() == false`.

Downsides: Any exchange header whose name matches a propagator field (e.g., `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `b3`) will be removed before a non-propagating send, even if the application placed it there deliberately. This is a deliberate trade-off: a non-propagating endpoint should not forward trace context regardless of where the header originated.

threads.body: [General] This clears only the globally configured propagator fields, but Camel stores an incoming SQS creation context under `AWSTraceHeader` and the new messaging propagator explicitly extracts that alias. In a stable SQS-to-SQS route, the old `AWSTraceHeader` therefore survives this branch and Camel can copy it as a message attribute alongside the nested SDK span's new system attribute, leaving consumers with conflicting creation contexts. Remove the Camel SQS alias here as well.

replies.body:
Addressed in 1977ef238d4520725dcb0a49bcf95836132f081c.

Analysis: The stable messaging path suppresses Camel propagation but only removed fields from the configured global propagator. Camel's `AWSTraceHeader` alias is outside that field set and remained available for downstream SQS propagation. Clear the alias explicitly and cover both the configured field and the Camel-specific alias in a unit test.

Upsides: Stable SQS-to-SQS routes cannot carry a stale Camel creation context alongside the nested AWS SDK span's system context. The unit test protects both clearing paths while confirming unrelated headers remain intact.

Downsides: Stable messaging sends that suppress propagation now remove `AWSTraceHeader` even when a custom component uses that name for another purpose.

threads.body: [General] This uses producer-style RabbitMQ destination formatting for inbound process spans as well. The migrated RabbitMQ instrumentation includes the queue when it differs from the routing key (`RabbitInstrumenterHelper.consumerDestinationName`, lines 115-122), but this method never reads Camel's `queue` endpoint option and returns `amq.default` even for an otherwise empty inbound destination. Pass the Camel direction into this extraction and apply the consumer formatting for inbound routes so, for example, `orders?routingKey=created&queue=workers` produces `orders:created:workers`.

replies.body: Fixed in efa3d09cfd. Stable RabbitMQ destination extraction now receives the Camel direction, includes a distinct queue for inbound process spans, returns `null` for an empty inbound destination, and applies `bridgeEndpoint` only to outbound sends. The destination tests now cover inbound queue formatting, matching queue/routing keys, empty inbound destinations, and direction-specific bridge behavior.
